city_params.n_celdas_hint: Spatial resolution: more cells = smoother profiles but slower simulation. Does not change the model physics (population is set by density × length).
city_params.n_parcelas_hint: Each parcel ≈ {{dx}} m wide (Δx = length/n). More parcels = higher spatial resolution (slower simulation). Total population is set by density × length, so it does NOT change with n.
city_params.densidad_hint: ≈ {{cuadra}} households per 100 m block · total population = density × length = {{total}}. Very high values saturate the network (gridlock).
city_params.pendiente_hint: Corridor slope: it slows the bike toward the CBD (uphill) and favors it on the way back.
city_params.land_use_note: Stratum composition and density are defined in Land Use and feed this simulation (per-stratum density → per-cell density).
city_params.defined_in_land_use: The city (length, cells, slope, density and strata) is defined in Land Use and feeds this simulation.
city_params.largo_hint: Population fixed ({{pob}} hh): changing the length recomputes density (now {{rho}} pop/km).

economy_params.bencina_hint: Small effect: drivers (high-income) are insensitive to per-km cost. To discourage cars, use parking (fixed cost) or road pricing.
economy_params.teletrabajo_hint: Scales each stratum’s telework rate (the base rate is set in Calibration). Those agents do not travel and leave peak demand: it is the only lever here that removes trips rather than reassigning them between modes.

car.num_pistas_hint: Only helps if cars are congested (high v/c). With low car demand, adding lanes barely changes anything.
car.cap_manual_hint: Fixed capacity: raising speed no longer increases it (S-04).
car.cap_greenshields: Greenshields capacity: {{cap}} veh/h per lane (∝ free-flow speed — raising v_max also raises capacity).

train.freq_clip_max: ⚠ Frequency CAPPED by max frequency at {{op}} tph — demand asks for {{teo}}. Raising it does change the result; lowering the minimum does nothing. The Mohring effect is exhausted: more riders no longer bring more trains.
train.freq_clip_min: ⚠ Frequency CAPPED by min frequency at {{op}} tph — demand only asks for {{teo}}. Lowering it does change the result; raising the maximum does nothing.
train.freq_clip_libre: Frequency free at {{op}} tph: demand sets it (load / train capacity). Neither cap is binding, so moving the minimum or maximum changes nothing until it crosses that value.
train.anden_hint: Platform congestion (BPR): penalizes waiting once load exceeds the max-frequency capacity (v/c>1).
train.num_estaciones_hint: More stations shorten the walk to the platform but lengthen the ride: the train stops at each one. There is an interior optimum.
train.costo_operacion_hint: PROVISIONAL, pending a source. Enables operator cost, subsidy and self-financing in the results table.
train.factor_dia_punta_hint: Self-financing compares DAILY cost against DAILY revenue, but the model simulates only the peak hour. This factor is how much more expensive it is to run the whole day, per trip, than if the whole day had the peak's load. Off-peak service runs emptier, hence greater than 1.

equilibrium.assignment_hint_montecarlo: Samples each agent's mode (stochastic; noisy across iterations).
equilibrium.assignment_hint_expected: Fractional assignment by logit probabilities (deterministic, noise-free).
equilibrium.modos_hint: Remove modes from the choice set to study stylized scenarios (e.g. Car vs Metro only).
equilibrium.modos_min: At least one mode must stay enabled.
equilibrium.verdict_ok: Converged in {{n}} of {{total}} iterations: the residual fell to {{res}} min, within the {{tol}} min tolerance. The results below are an equilibrium.
equilibrium.verdict_fail: Ran out of {{total}} iterations without converging: the residual stayed at {{res}} min, above the {{tol}} min tolerance. Travel times are still moving, so what follows is NOT an equilibrium and cannot be used to compare scenarios. Raise the iteration cap or loosen the tolerance.
equilibrium.verdict_no_tol: No convergence criterion (tolerance 0): it ran the fixed {{total}} iterations and stopped by count, not because travel times settled. The final residual is {{res}} min.
equilibrium.booting_pyodide: Initializing Pyodide in the browser (first run takes ~10–20s)…
equilibrium.assignment_hint_todo_o_nada: DETERMINISTIC choice: each group goes entirely to the highest-utility mode, with no taste heterogeneity. It is the logit limit as the coefficient scale grows. It does NOT equalize costs across modes: on the default city all four modes are used at once with costs differing by up to 32 min, and 91% of groups sit far from indifference (scripts/auditoria_wardrop.py). What changes is that the marginal group switches AS A WHOLE. Careful: it can have multiple equilibria, because the metro's waiting time falls as it gains demand, violating the increasing-cost condition that guarantees uniqueness.
equilibrium.kpis_sin_equilibrio: ⚠ The run did not converge: the figures below are NOT an equilibrium and cannot be used to compare scenarios. See the verdict further down.

presets.diff_hint: {{n}} parameter(s) differ from the base scenario (marked ↑/↓). Grey rows are at their base value.
presets.no_diff_hint: Base scenario: no parameter differs from the default.
presets.presets_hint: City presets change only the length and keep population: they compare urban form, not demand size.

sandbox.flow_replay_hint: Corridor flow is the sum of the trips originating in each cell, accumulated toward the CBD. That is why it grows toward the centre and can exceed capacity even when no single cell comes close to it.
sandbox.mode_share_by_location_stratum: Modal split by location and stratum
sandbox.city_figure_desc: Linear city of {{length}} km with {{cells}} cells. CBD at center. Bar height and color scale with travel time on {{mode}}.
sandbox.utility_caveat: Utilities are in each stratum's own utils (different ASC and β): comparing heights ACROSS strata is not valid — only within a stratum and across modes.
sandbox.city_view_caption: Above, who lives in each cell (land use); below, what was built on it (supply). They share the position axis, so the same cell falls in the same column in both figures. These are the two inputs to the equilibrium.
sandbox.land_use_city_desc: Household distribution by stratum along the {{length}} km linear city ({{cells}} cells), as defined by the Land Use module. CBD at center.
sandbox.land_use_city_caption_post: Equilibrium composition from the Land Use module (S·Q). This is the city that feeds the transport simulation.
sandbox.land_use_city_caption_pre: Initial composition (uniform π_h mix over the city shape). Run Land Use to see the equilibrium composition.
sandbox.land_use_city_caption_none: Define the population in the Land Use module to see the distribution by stratum.

metrics_table.vc_metro_sub: max load / (max freq x train capacity)
metrics_table.network_load_note: Car and bike: peak corridor flow over capacity; >1 means running above capacity. Metro differs: frequency adapts to demand (f_op = load/K), so its ratio is 1 unless the frec_max ceiling or frec_min floor binds — >1 means insufficient frequency, not crowding (the model has no in-vehicle crowding penalty). All three respond to population, prices and capacity, NOT to city length: in a monocentric city the section next to the CBD carries about half the trips regardless of extent.

hero.title: The linear city
hero.subtitle: Mode share by location · 0 km = west edge · center = CBD

hints.demand_body: Each cell has three strata (High / Mid / Low). Telework is decided beforehand and does not travel; everyone else chooses among the enabled modes that are feasible for them (walking ≤ 30 min, cycling ≤ 45 min, car only with ownership). By default the split is a multinomial logit over times and costs; under deterministic assignment the whole group goes to the highest-utility mode.
hints.supply_body: Car: capacity from Greenshields (lane width reduces it) and BPR delay accumulated toward the CBD. Bike: same volume/capacity form, corrected for slope and floored at walking time. Metro: frequency endogenous to the critical link (capped by frec_min/frec_max), half-headway wait amplified by platform saturation, and intermediate stops inside the in-vehicle time — more stations shorten access but lengthen the ride.
hints.equilibrium_body: MSA alternates demand ↔ supply averaging travel times with step 1/k, which damps the oscillation of iterating without averaging. The residual is the largest time change in any mode and cell; it converges when that stays below tolerance for 2 consecutive iterations (with tolerance 0 it runs to the iteration cap).

calibration.title: Model calibration
calibration.not_a_policy: Not a policy. These are the estimated logit coefficients: moving them changes the behavioural model, not the city or the supply. A scenario where car use fell because its constant was edited says nothing about transport policy.
calibration.ratio_hint: Value of time is β time ÷ β cost. The ratios say how many times more onerous a minute of waiting —or of walking to the station— is than a minute in the vehicle. Chile's 2026 social prices (SNI) assign weight 2 to both; below 1 the model claims waiting bothers people less than travelling.
calibration.b_costo_warn: β cost must be negative: at 0 or positive, the value of time and the surplus are undefined.
calibration.g_asc_hint: They capture everything the model does not measure (comfort, habit, status). Only differences between modes matter: adding the same amount to all four changes nothing.
calibration.g_tiempo_hint: In utils per minute and per peso. All negative: more time or more money, less utility. Metro access and the walking mode use SEPARATE coefficients: the walk to a station is not the same as walking the whole trip. There is a single cost β covering fuel, fare and parking together.
calibration.g_penal_hint: Additive, cumulative and triggered by MINUTE thresholds: a 25-min bike trip adds both the 10-min and the 20-min penalty. Above 45 min cycling is infeasible; walking, above 30 min.
calibration.prob_teletrabajo_hint: Base rate for the stratum. The telework policy is the multiplier, under “Economy”.
calibration.cortes_hint: Above this time the alternative leaves the choice set: it does not get a large penalty, it stops existing for that trip. It is a behavioural assumption, not a transport policy. These are global —they do not vary by stratum— and moving a cutoff changes how many alternatives there are, so it also moves the gap between logsum and max-utility surplus.

demand_inspector.title: Utility inspector — multinomial logit
demand_inspector.interpretation: V = the mode's systematic utility, the observed part of U = V + ε. It is in utils: only differences across modes matter — ~1 util of advantage ≈ 2.7× more likely. P = choice probability of THIS agent (not the system's mode share).
demand_inspector.todo_o_nada_notice: Deterministic assignment is active: the simulation sends the WHOLE group to the mode with the highest V, with no splitting. These P values are the logit ones — use them to read the utility function, not to anticipate this run's mode split.

utility_breakdown.v_title: V — the mode's systematic utility, in utils
utility_breakdown.p_title: P — choice probability of this agent

stratum_distribution.aria: Spatial distribution of households by stratum

land_use.title: Land use
land_use.poblacion_total_hint: Total population ≈ {{total}} = length × mean density ({{dens}} pop/km). It sets how many households there are; per-cell density is a consequence of supply (S/Δx), not an imposed gradient.
land_use.bidrent_hint: Auction sensitivities: α (time) and ρ (density) per stratum set the spatial ordering (who wins the center); β (global) scales the choice noise. Income y does NOT move the allocation: it is absorbed into equilibrium utility. λ does move it, but as an artifact: it rescales that stratum's α, ρ and noise all at once.
land_use.subtitle: Alonso-Muth-Mills model
land_use.info_standalone: Solves the Alonso equilibrium with T = free-flow time to the CBD (30 km/h, no congestion).
land_use.info_coupled: Iterates land use ↔ transport until T stabilizes.
land_use.density_ignored_hint: In coupled mode, per-cell population comes from the land-use assignment (Σ H = {{total}}); the Transport tab's «Density per cell» slider is ignored.
land_use.outer_iter_hint: Each iteration runs the full transport MSA. Keep small in class.
land_use.run_placeholder: Run the solver to see the spatial assignment.
land_use.heading_distribution: Spatial distribution of households by stratum
land_use.heatmap_caption: Per-cell strata composition. Before the equilibrium every cell has the same mix (global proportions); bid-rent sorts it: the stratum that values the center most wins the parcels near the CBD. Total households per cell are set by the housing supply and do not change with the equilibrium; only who lives where.
land_use.densidad_hint: Characteristic residential density of the stratum. Each cell's density is derived from its composition: Σ_h Q[h,i]·δ_h.
land_use.oferta_sigma_hint: Shape of housing supply: low = compact city (near CBD), high = sprawling.
land_use.forma_hint_normal: Bell centered on the CBD: compact monocentric.
land_use.forma_hint_uniforme: Flat density along the whole corridor (homogeneous suburb).
land_use.forma_hint_exponencial: Density ∝ e^(−d/σ): decays from the CBD (von Thünen).
land_use.forma_hint_bimodal: Two peaks: polycentric city with subcenters.
land_use.forma_hint_meseta: Flat-density core with a sharp edge: compact city with a boundary.
land_use.shape_preview_caption: Housing supply profile S(d) for the current parameters. Run the equilibrium to see how the strata sort over this city.
land_use.initial_pop_caption: Initial state (pre-equilibrium): every cell has the SAME strata proportion (the global proportions), over the supply profile S(d). Run the equilibrium: bid-rent sorts this uniform mix in space (strata that value the center most win the parcels near the CBD).
land_use.metrics_caption: Mean distance to the CBD by stratum (bid-rent test: the highest-valuation stratum wins the center) · Theil segregation (0 = mixed, 1 = fully segregated)
land_use.forma_hint_valle: Little space at the center, lots at the periphery: density grows with distance (inverted triangle).
land_use.oferta_sigma_na: Not applicable to the uniform shape (flat density).
land_use.lambda_artifact_logit: With λ differing across strata the core switches on its own to the heteroskedastic auction (HEV, Train §4.5): there λ IS identified, because besides the bid it moves the noise scale. Still mind this: it enters through two channels at once — lower λ raises α_eff = α/λ, so the stratum values access more and moves toward the CBD. It is not price sensitivity: in an auction the price cancels between bidders. Income y, by contrast, reallocates nobody.
land_use.y_na: Does not affect the allocation: income enters only as a per-stratum constant and is absorbed into the equilibrium utility. Sorting is governed by α and ρ.
land_use.intro: Bid-rent theory predicts that households with the highest valuation of accessibility to the center outbid the rest for parcels near the CBD, pushing lower-valuation groups toward the periphery.
land_use.relation: This module solves land use ONLY, with transport fixed at free flow. For the full land ↔ transport loop, see “City at equilibrium”.
land_use.placeholder_title: Land use · the auction for space
land_use.placeholder_desc: The Alonso equilibrium allocates households by auction: each stratum bids for parcels according to its valuation of accessibility (α·T) and its disutility of density (ρ·dens). The stratum that values proximity the most wins the center; the rest sort toward the periphery. Adjust the city shape and per-stratum parameters on the left panel.

coupled.title: City at equilibrium
coupled.lede: Transport and land use are not independent systems. Congestion reshuffles households; the new locations change demand; demand reshapes the network. This page lets you run a joint scenario and compare the naive equilibrium (no feedback) with the coupled one (with feedback).
coupled.placeholder: Select a scenario and press «Run scenario».
coupled.without_feedback_hint: First pass of the coupled loop: land use is solved with travel times equal to distance, unaware of congestion.
coupled.with_feedback_hint: Reconciled equilibrium: land and transport iterate mutually until stable. Differences reveal the feedback effect.
coupled.source_preset_label: Or try a predefined scenario (quick test)
coupled.custom_desc: Run the loop with the city you set up in the Transport and Land Use modules.
coupled.preset_detail_hint: These are the parameters the preset moves: they define whether the city is compact or sprawling, and whether the policy favors cars, bikes or the metro.
coupled.preset_detail_hint_custom: These parameters come from your Transport (Sandbox) and Land Use modules. To change them, adjust them in those modules and come back here.
coupled.convergence_hint: The loop alternates land and transport. The residual ‖ΔT‖∞ measures how much travel times change between iterations; as it tends to 0, the system reaches a mutual equilibrium. The slider shows how the city reshuffles at each step.

sparse_proauto.desc: Sprawled city with abundant road infra. US scenario.

base_probici.desc: Medium city with wide bike lanes and disincentivized parking.

compact_metro.title: Compact + Max Metro
compact_metro.desc: Dense city with maximum metro frequency and many stations.

interp.segregation_up: Feedback increased segregation by Δ={{delta}}. Congestion pushes high-time-value strata to the center; low-value ones migrate to the periphery.
interp.segregation_down: Feedback reduced segregation by Δ={{delta}}. Spatial reshuffle diluted the initial stratum concentration.
interp.welfare_regressive: Regressive effect: the low stratum's monthly transport burden changed {{bajo}} pp (now {{cargaBajo}}% of its income) while the high stratum's changed {{alto}} pp. The feedback weighs relatively more on the vulnerable.
interp.welfare_progressive: Progressive effect: the low stratum's monthly burden changed {{bajo}} pp (now {{cargaBajo}}% of its income) vs {{alto}} pp for the high stratum. The feedback relieves the vulnerable relatively more.
interp.accessibility_body: Relative to the no-feedback start, the high stratum's mean travel time changed {{alto}} min and the low stratum's {{bajo}} min. The low stratum ends up traveling {{tBajo}} min on average.
interp.stable_body: Outer iterations did not meaningfully shift aggregate metrics. Feedback was weak in this scenario — try a more aggressive policy.

coupled.placeholder_desc: The outer loop alternates three steps: (1) bid-rent allocates households given accessibility T(i), (2) that population runs the transport equilibrium (MSA), (3) the new travel times update T. It iterates until T stabilizes.
coupled.poblacion_warn: ⚠ Above ~{{n}}k this scenario saturates the corridor (gridlock): travel times become unrealistic and the equilibrium degrades. Useful to observe collapse, not as a realistic scenario.

coupled_metrics.segregation_hint: Theil index. 0 = integrated city, 1 = perfect segregation. Drops when policy brings strata together; rises if the market pulls them apart.
coupled_metrics.welfare_hint: Average chosen-mode utility per stratum. Rises under policies that reduce time or cost for the average agent.
coupled_metrics.accessibility_hint: Hansen index per stratum: Σ exp(−α·T). Larger = destinations closer in generalized cost. Compare deltas, not absolute values.

eqt.title: Equilibrium metrics
eqt.cs_max: Δ Surplus (max utility) vs empty network
eqt.delta_note: Δ = change vs iteration 0 (no feedback). Metrics tagged «input» are scenario data and do not change with feedback.
eqt.welfare_total_sub: Σ households · ΔCS vs empty network ($)
eqt.caveat: The surplus Δ compares the observed logsum against the same network with zero demand (BPR at 0, train at minimum frequency): Δ<0 ⇒ congestion dominates; Δ>0 ⇒ the Mohring effect dominates (more demand ⇒ higher frequency ⇒ less waiting). It is in $ as efficiency / willingness to pay, NOT interpersonal welfare: $1 is worth differently to each stratum (b_costo varies ~7.5×). For the distributional reading, look at the burden (cost/income) and time. The table's Δ is vs iteration 0 (no feedback).

convergence.modal_split_sub: Evolution of modal split while MSA smooths (cumulative trips per mode)

network.title: Road network · saturation by segment
network.aria: Linear city road network with auto, metro and bike

msa.aria: Interactive diagram of the MSA algorithm
msa.initial_desc: First iteration: agents assume no congestion. Times = distance / free-flow speed.
msa.logit_desc: Each agent evaluates utility per mode and chooses with probability proportional to exp(V_m).
msa.congestion_desc: Given assigned demand, times are recomputed with BPR (auto, bike) or platform saturation (metro).
msa.smooth_desc: To avoid oscillation, the new T is averaged with prior ones: weight f_n = 1/(n+1) decays with n.
msa.check_desc: If iteration-to-iteration variation falls below threshold, equilibrium is reached.
msa.done_desc: Travel times are consistent with the modal assignment they induce.

coupled.aria: Interactive diagram of the land-use↔transport coupled loop
coupled.config_desc: City, strata, infrastructure and land-use parameters. Initial T = distance to CBD.
coupled.landuse_desc: Solves the Alonso equilibrium: each stratum gets a distribution Q over parcels balancing price, accessibility and density.
coupled.assign_desc: From Q, concrete households are drawn per parcel respecting the supply S_i.
coupled.transport_desc: With the new population, a full transport equilibrium runs; its output is a new T[h, i] matrix.
coupled.check_desc: T is compared to the previous outer iteration. Tolerance on the order of 1 minute.
coupled.done_desc: Land use and transport are consistent: neither changes when the other is updated.

agg.viajes_fisicos_nota: (denominator of the split below; excludes telework)
agg.medida_utilidad_maxima: Under the deterministic method surplus is measured with mean maximum utility, not the logsum: with no taste dispersion the agent takes the best mode and its E[max] is that maximum. The logsum would overstate it by the value the logit assigns to variety.
agg.medida_incomparable: ⚠ The reference was run with a different assignment method: the two surplus figures use different definitions, so the level is shown but not the Δ.
agg.intro_sin_ref: City-wide aggregates. Pin this run as the reference to compare the next one against it.
agg.intro_con_ref: Δ against the pinned reference. Green = improvement, red = worse.
agg.vot_hint: Implied value of time (β_time/β_cost): high {{alto}}/h · mid {{medio}}/h · low {{bajo}}/h. The social cost uses a single value so as not to weight by income.
agg.logsum_incomparable: ⚠ The scenarios do not share the same mode set: surplus is not comparable between them (the logsum changes scale).
agg.title: Aggregates and comparison
agg.recaudacion_nota: (transfers; fuel excluded: it is real resource use)
agg.bienestar: Social welfare = surplus + revenue − operating cost
agg.bienestar_nota: (cost per train-km is provisional; see docs)
agg.caption: City-wide aggregates
agg.excedente_social_nota: (valued at the social VoT {{vot}}/h instead of each stratum’s behavioural one: everyone’s minute is worth the same)
agg.escenario_hint: Presets describing this run, recognised from their parameters. “Custom” = matches none.
agg.reparto_hint: Mode shares and their Δ are in percentage points over physical trips. The Δ is not coloured: a mode going up is not an improvement by itself —it depends at whose expense—.
agg.unidades_hint: Monetary figures are city-wide totals except those marked (person), which are the per-traveller mean of the stratum. The LEVEL of surplus is not interpretable —its zero is set by the ASCs—; only the Δ is.

espera.base_nota: Half the headway: 30 / {{f}} tph. This is the channel that rules at this population: if demand falls, frequency falls and waiting rises.
espera.anden_inactivo: Inactive: at ρ = {{rho}} the surcharge is negligible. Far more demand would be needed for the platform to matter.
espera.anden_activo: Active: at ρ = {{rho}} the platform adds {{pct}} % to waiting.
espera.constante: Waiting is the SAME along the whole line: one frequency for the service and a platform surcharge that does not bite, so a spatial profile would draw a straight line.
espera.varia: Ranges from {{min}} to {{max}} min by station ({{pct}} %): each one carries a different load.
espera.msa_nota: The figure above is the equilibrium one and does not exactly match 30/f_op because the MSA averages times across iterations.
